blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: With `enum Size { S, M, L }`, a method declares `String label;`, then runs `switch (size) { case S -> label = "small"; case M -> label = "medium"; case L -> label = "large"; }` and ends with `return label;`. What does javac do with it?

options.text: It compiles, since each of the three constants has an arm that assigns label
options.says: a switch statement over an enum is not treated as covering every constant, so naming them all doesn't make label definitely assigned

options.text: It compiles, since arrow labels make javac check that the arms cover Size
options.says: arrows decide only that there is no fall-through; the coverage check belongs to switch expressions

options.text: It refuses it, since javac doesn't treat a statement over Size as covering every constant
options.says: a switch statement may skip a constant and run nothing, so javac reports that label might not have been initialized

options.text: It refuses it, since an arrow arm in a switch statement can't hold an assignment
options.says: an assignment is a statement, which is what an arrow arm in a switch statement must be

origin.section: A Switch Expression Is a Value, So Every Arm Must Produce One

questions.stem: A converter runs `Number n = switch (unit) { case "kg" -> 1; default -> 0.5; };` with `unit` equal to "kg", then tests `n instanceof Integer`. What does the test give?

options.text: true, since an int arm is boxed to Integer when the switch is assigned to Number
options.says: assigned to a reference type, the switch takes the target type and each arm is boxed separately, so 1 becomes an Integer

options.text: true, since an int arm is boxed to Integer whatever type the other arms have
options.says: under var, with no target type, the same arms are promoted to double, so the other arms do matter

options.text: false, since the int arm is promoted to double first, as in a numeric ?:
options.says: that promotion happens to a numeric ?: and to a switch with no target type, such as one under var, not to one assigned to Number

options.text: false, since the int arm is promoted to double first, as in any mixed switch
options.says: a switch with mixed numeric arms promotes them only when it has no target type, such as under var; assigned to Number, each arm is boxed on its own

origin.section: A Switch Expression Is a Value, So Every Arm Must Produce One

questions.stem: `int fee = switch (zone) { case LOCAL: yield 5; case ISLAND: surcharges.add("ferry"); case REMOTE: yield 20; default: yield 10; };` runs with `zone` equal to ISLAND. What happens?

options.text: fee is 20 and the ferry surcharge is added, since ISLAND runs on into REMOTE
options.says: a colon label falls through in a switch expression as in a statement, so ISLAND continues into REMOTE

options.text: fee is 10 and the ferry surcharge is added, since ISLAND runs on into default
options.says: execution continues with the next case in the source, which is REMOTE, not with default

options.text: It doesn't compile, since the ISLAND case ends without a yield of its own
options.says: with colon labels a case may run on into the next one; only a switch rule (arrow) must give a value or throw

options.text: It doesn't compile, since a switch expression needs arrow labels on its cases
options.says: a switch expression may use colon labels, ending cases with yield; what javac refuses is mixing arrows and colons in one switch

origin.section: An Arrow Label Runs One Arm and Never Falls Through; a Colon Label Still Does, Even in an Expression

questions.stem: A shipping service compiled with `--release 21` maps a library's `Region` enum to a carrier name in a switch expression that names all four regions. The library is upgraded with a fifth region and the service is not recompiled. A parcel for the new region arrives. What does the call do?

options.text: It throws MatchException, from a default arm that javac added to the switch
options.says: for a switch expression over an enum with no default, javac adds a default that throws MatchException when compiled for release 21

options.text: It throws NullPointerException, from a lookup that finds no arm for the region
options.says: the generated default throws MatchException; NullPointerException comes from a null selector

options.text: It returns the last arm's carrier, since an unmatched region runs the arm written last
options.says: an unmatched constant runs no arm; it reaches the throwing default javac generated

options.text: It returns null, since an unmatched region leaves the switch without a carrier
options.says: a switch expression never completes without a value; the generated default throws instead

origin.section: A Constant Added After Compilation Reaches the Switch as MatchException

concepts: A switch statement over an enum is not treated as covering every constant, so a variable it assigns in every arm is still not definitely assigned; a switch expression gives one value with no default.
Assigned to a reference type, a switch expression boxes each arm on its own, while a numeric ?: and a switch under var promote the arms to a common numeric type.
